steps.title: Guidance
steps.body: The help and direction given to a performer to assist them in learning and developing skills. Coaches use different types of guidance to support performers at different stages of learning and for different types of skill.

steps.title: Visual Guidance
steps.body: Showing the performer how to perform a skill through demonstrations, videos, or diagrams. The performer watches and copies the correct technique.

steps.title: Verbal Guidance
steps.body: Explaining how to perform a skill using spoken instructions, coaching points, or cue words. The performer listens and interprets the information.

steps.title: Manual Guidance
steps.body: The coach physically moves, supports or guides the performer's body to help them experience the correct movement. This provides kinaesthetic awareness of the skill.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe the four types of guidance used in sport and give a sporting example of each. | Explain why visual guidance is particularly effective for beginners in the cognitive stage of learning. | What is the main disadvantage of manual guidance and how can a coach address this?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always give a sporting example when describing each type of guidance Link guidance type to the stage of learning - beginners vs elite Remember to discuss both advantages and disadvantages for each type Use the term "fading" when discussing how manual/mechanical guidance should be gradually removed Verbal guidance for beginners = short cue words only; for elite = detailed technical adjustments Manual and mechanical both address safety and kinaesthetic awareness but differ in delivery method
